diagnosis: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL), not otherwise specified (NOS). ICD-10-CM: C83.30; SNOMED CT: 109969005. Confirmed by left axillary lymph node biopsy demonstrating architectural effacement by large atypical lymphoid cells expressing CD20 (+), BCL6 (+), MUM1 (+), and negative CD10 (-), with a high proliferative index (Ki-67 80%). Evidence-based reasoning: Pathologic synoptic report and immunohistochemistry definitively establish DLBCL. Uncertainty: Distinction between de novo DLBCL versus transformed indolent lymphoma cannot be definitively excluded without prior history, though none is documented.
stage: Ann Arbor Stage III-B (Lugano Stage III). Evidence-based reasoning: Baseline 18F-FDG PET-CT demonstrates FDG-avid lymphadenopathy above the diaphragm (left axillary, mediastinal) and below the diaphragm (mesenteric, para-aortic), alongside extranodal splenic involvement (FDG-avid splenic nodules). The largest nodal mass measures 7.5 cm (bulky disease depending on institutional cutoff, typically >7-10 cm). B-symptoms (intermittent fevers) are present. Bone marrow biopsy is negative for lymphoma involvement. Uncertainty: Splenic involvement designates Stage III per Ann Arbor staging rules (spleen as lymphatic organ), but confers an aggressive clinical presentation similar to visceral extranodal disease.
biology: Non-GCB (Activated B-cell-like, ABC) subtype by Hans algorithm (CD10-, BCL6+, MUM1+). Double-Expressor Lymphoma (DEL) characterized by overexpression of BCL2 (70%) and c-MYC (45%) by immunohistochemistry. FISH analysis shows no MYC, BCL2, or BCL6 gene rearrangements, ruling out Double-Hit or Triple-Hit High-Grade B-Cell Lymphoma (HGBL). Evidence-based reasoning: IHC and FISH synoptic reports provide clear cell-of-origin and translocation status. Uncertainty: While FISH ruled out structural translocations, the combination of non-GCB/ABC phenotype and double-expressor protein overexpression (BCL2>=50%, MYC>=40%) confers a higher risk of chemoresistance and inferior survival compared to GCB germline DLBCL.
prognosis: Intermediate Risk (Standard International Prognostic Index [IPI] score of 2, or NCCN-IPI score of 3). Evidence-based reasoning: Risk factors present include elevated LDH (510 U/L), Ann Arbor Stage III, and extranodal (splenic) involvement. Age (59 years) and ECOG performance status (1) are favorable/non-elevated points in standard IPI. Adverse biological features (non-GCB/ABC subtype, double-expressor protein overexpression, high Ki-67 80%) convey additional biological risk beyond standard clinical scoring. Uncertainty: Traditional clinical scoring models (IPI/NCCN-IPI) do not fully capture the negative prognostic impact of non-GCB ABC subtype and double-expressor status in the absence of MYC/BCL2 translocations.
first_line_treatment: Polatuzumab vedotin combined with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone (Pola-R-CHP) for 6 cycles, or standard R-CHOP for 6 cycles. Evidence-based reasoning: Pola-R-CHP is a category 1 preferred regimen for intermediate/high-risk DLBCL (IPI 2-5) based on superior progression-free survival demonstrated in the POLARIX trial compared to R-CHOP. Primary G-CSF prophylaxis is recommended. Uncertainty: Choosing between Pola-R-CHP and R-CHOP requires weighing improved PFS against potential cumulative peripheral neuropathy risk and resource availability; patient comorbidities (e.g. baseline neuropathy) must be evaluated.
cns_risk: Low-to-Intermediate CNS-relapse risk by NCCN CNS-IPI. Evidence-based reasoning: Factors present include Stage III and elevated LDH, offset by age <60, ECOG 1, single extranodal site (spleen), and absence of high-risk anatomic involvement (PET-CT explicitly confirms no kidney, adrenal, testicular, breast, or epidural lesions). Routine CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal or systemic high-dose methotrexate) is generally not recommended for low-to-intermediate CNS-IPI risk patients. Uncertainty: The presence of double-expressor biology and non-GCB subtype theoretically elevates aggressive potential, but guidelines do not mandate CNS prophylaxis in the absence of high CNS-IPI score or high-risk anatomic sites.
response_assessment: End-of-treatment (and optional interim after cycle 2 or 4) 18F-FDG PET-CT evaluated using Lugano 2014 criteria via the Deauville 5-Point Scale (5PS). Evidence-based reasoning: Standard of care response criteria for DLBCL. Complete Metabolic Response (CMR) is defined as a Deauville score of 1, 2, or 3 in all previously involved sites. Uncertainty: False-positive PET findings due to post-inflammatory uptake, thymic rebound, or therapy-related tissue reaction can occur (Deauville 4); confirmation with biopsy or serial imaging may be required for equivocal residual uptake.
missing_information: 1. Baseline cardiac evaluation (left ventricular ejection fraction via echocardiogram or MUGA scan) prior to anthracycline (doxorubicin) administration. 2. Hepatitis B serology panel (HBsAg, anti-HBc total, anti-HBs) for rituximab-associated reactivation screening. 3. Comprehensive baseline metabolic panel including renal function (creatinine clearance / eGFR) and hepatic transaminases/bilirubin for chemotherapeutic dose adjustments. 4. HIV serology and baseline serum albumin / beta-2 microglobulin for precise NCCN-IPI refinement. Evidence-based reasoning: Standard pre-treatment safety and staging workup items required for safe initiation of immunochemotherapy are absent from the FHIR bundle.
